articleTitle: Super-Resolution of Multiple Sentinel-2 Images Using Composite Loss Function
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: In the current domain of image super-resolution (SR), particularly concerning satellite imagery processing based on mainstream deep learning methodologies, most algorithms typically employ loss functions such as L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> loss (Mean Absolute Error) or L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> loss (Mean Squared Error) based on pixel value differences when training network models. However, when magnifying the details of the resulting images, there is often a blurring effect at the edges where different ground conditions, such as city roads, buildings, and various terrains, intersect, making it difficult to distinguish the edges of these different objects. On the other hand, in our previous experiments, using the Perceptual Loss function (based on calculating perceptual error of images) for training models yielded images with improved visual quality, allowing for better object distinction. Nevertheless, although the object edges did not appear blurred, the transitions at the edges were somewhat abrupt and distorted. Therefore, in this paper, a composite loss function that combines L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> loss and Perceptual Loss is proposed, aiming to leverage their advantages to enhance the visual quality of objects in satellite images while avoiding edge blurring and achieving higher object discrimination. Additionally, we continue to explore the optimization of the SGNET (Sentinel-2 Google-Earth-Pro Network) architecture to improve the image super-resolution results.

articleTitle: Step-by-Step Design of a LLC Resonant Converter for EV Fast Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: Electric mobility is already well established in societies, but there are still several technological challenges to overcome. Specifically, a key challenge is the concern about charging systems, which should be faster and more efficient. In this context, regarding the DC-DC back-end power stage, a special emphasis is given to LLC resonant power converters. Aligned with this context, this paper presents a step-by-step design and description of a LLC resonant power converter. MATLAB and PSIM simulation models were developed for validating, respectively, the gain design of the LCC tank and the analysis of the operation considering such different designs. For validation purposes, an input voltage of 900 V, an output voltage of 900 V, and a resonant frequency of 100 kHz were considered. The validating results were obtained for different conditions of operation, according to the different designs, showing a maximum estimated efficiency of 99.5%.

articleTitle: Shunt Active Power Filter Applied To Four-wire Electrical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: This work presents the study and implementation of a three-phase four-wire shunt active power filter applied to electrical network, aiming to reduce the power quality problems associated with current harmonic distortion, power factor and unbalance. The determination of the compensation currents reference is performed using the instantaneous powers theory (p-q theory). The results obtained with the methodology employed are proven through numerical simulations and validated by experimental data using a 10kVA prototype implemented in the ISEL Electrical Machines Laboratory. The use of the shunt active power filter provided the reduction of the harmonic content of the non-linear loads employed in the tests, as well as the power factor improvement to practically unity values, reduced current in the neutral wire, and unbalance of the currents. This simulation analysis shows that this system complies with energy quality standards.

articleTitle: Economic Feasibility of Production Units for Self-Consumption with Storage Batteries to Charge Electric Vehicles: Case Study in the Residential Portuguese Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: The transition to sustainable energy is vital for the responsible use and development of resources, including the integration of renewable energies in residential and industrial sectors and the promotion of electric mobility. These initiatives are essential pillars in achieving the energy and environmental goals defined by the European Union and Portugal. In this paper, a case study was carried out, applied to the residential Portuguese sector, about the economic feasibility of Production Units for Self-Consumption with storage batteries and the possibility of charging electric vehicles. Different scenarios were analyzed: individual self-consumption without storage batteries and individual self-consumption with storage batteries, including two distinct electric vehicles. According to the obtained results, there were significant reductions in energy imports from the electrical grid and, under certain conditions, the economic feasibility of the system was also achieved, which contribute to the sustainable use of resources.

articleTitle: A methodology for creating power system models from open source data
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: Open data solutions as OpenStreetMaps offer are based on crowdsourcing approaches, these contain a lot of information regarding critical infrastructures, including power networks. This paper describes a method based on freely accessible data such as those offered by OpenStreetMap to develop a framework that uses this type of information to create power system models for steady state simulations. A model obtained for a specified region was tested in one scenario with official data from a Portuguese transmission system operator. The results of this test led to the conclusion that it is feasible to effectively model the network using these services, albeit under specific conditions.

articleTitle: CBP detection using template matching to compute the solar rotation profile
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: Using images from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)/Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) instrument, this project employs computer vision techniques to study solar differential rotation. Coronal Bright Points (CBPs), serve as reliable tracers across multiple images due to their widespread distribution across latitudes, independence from the solar cycle, and distinct shape. Using an image matching algorithm, these CBPs were detected and tracked, demonstrating consistent performance throughout various solar cycle stages. Solar rotation values were calculated based on the movements of CBPs during their lifetime as a result of the performed tracking. A dedicated website was created in order to make the results available to anyone interested in this topic, providing near real-time information. Performance metrics of the tool, including its effectiveness during both low and high solar activity phases are showcased, demonstrating its utility across different solar conditions, as well as the impact of the detection performance on the speed rotation results and a comparison between the proposed detection method and Gradient Path Labelling (GPL).

articleTitle: Design of a 300mV-Supply Schmitt-Trigger-Based DIGOTA for GBW and DC Gain Enhancement in 16nm FinFET
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: An ultra-low voltage and power Schmitt-Trigger-Based Digital Operational Transconductance Amplifier (ST-DIGOTA) is proposed here for the first time using 16 nm CMOS FinFET technology. In this design, the inverter gates, whose digital outputs are used to govern the circuit evolution throughout each circuit states, are replaced by Schmitt-Trigger inverters making their own trip points variable. It allows the DIGOTA to stay more time in the states that trigger the output stage increasing then the circuit bandwidth. Similar to others digital-like OTA implementations, the proposed one is designed without the need of any biasing circuit and only used digital standard cells aiming a quick design cycle and porting. For comparison purpose, two DIGOTAs are designed at the same FinFET technology: with (ST-DIGOTA) and without (DIGOTA) Schmitt-Trigger inverters. Even though the ST-DIGOTA floorplan silicon area is 39% larger than DIGOTA, operating at the same supply voltage of only 300 mV, the ST-DIGOTA achieves 70% more Gain-bandwidth product (GBW) and 25dB more DC gain consuming only 451 nW more. Both OTAs are able to drive a capacitive load of 500pF having similar an average slew rate of 2.9 mV/μs for both the ST-DIGOTA and DIGOTA. In light of these results, an area-normalized large signal figure of merit (FOM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">LA</inf>) of 36k and 352.6k [(V/μs)·pF/(μW·mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)] are accomplished along with an area-normalized small signal figure of merit (FOM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SA</inf>) of 0.34M and 1.8M [MHz·pF/(μW·mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)] for ST-DIGOTA and DIGOTA, respectively.

articleTitle: Imaging with Capacitive Sensors Arrays for Powder Bed Fusion Quality Control
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: “This work evaluates the use of multiple capacitive sensors to provide layer-wise imaging results for in-situ quality control during powder bed fusion additive manufacturing. This new probe is capable of detecting different surface features produced by laser powder bed fusion with stainless steel 316.A probe, with a measurement accuracy better than 1 fF, an update rate of 37 ms, and 12 sensors distributed in a linear arrangement with a distance of 0.4 mm between them, allows for imaging while performing single pass scans.”

articleTitle: An Active Self-Interference Cancellation Front-end for Stepped-Frequency Continuous-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: This work presents the development of a Stepped- Frequency Continuous Wave (SFCW) radar with active self-interference cancellation (SIC), for the UHF band up to 3 GHz. The radar is monostatic with separate Transmission (TX) and Receiving (RX) antennas, with passive cancellation through isolation between the TX and RX antennas. The active cancellation is done with an RF modulator that generates a cancelling signal in phase opposition to the self-interference (SI), reducing its impact in the target detection. By using two independent local oscillators, the receiver architecture is configurable for homodyne or heterodyne. With the prototype, a passive antenna isolation of approximately 30 dB and a SIC of 17 dB, through the adjustment of the cancelling signal’s amplitude and phase, were demonstrated, for a total cancelling of 47 dB.

articleTitle: Impact of Vehicle-to-Grid Technologies on the Electricity System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: Currently, one of the main concerns revolves around environmental protection, particularly the urgent need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. In order to solve this problem, the emission of the greenhouse gases needs to reduce. As a response to this obligation the transportation sector needs to be reformed.Despite the fact electric vehicles be one of the solutions, growing without care can create problems, more specifically in the electrical grid. It can cause serious problems, in the worst case power supply failure due to unbalanced demand/supply from the electrical grid. This is where the V2G (Vehicle-to-Grid) appears. This technology can have many benefits and take the care needed to this type of changing and evolution. This technology allow the use of the energy stored in the batteries of EVs for the benefit of the electrical system, allowing the provision of services to the grid.This paper aims to study the impact that these technologies have on the grid, as well the study of possibles services that can be provided, at the global level of the electrical system. To achieve this, data collection will be carried out. This data will be analyzed and a forecast will be considered to study the evolution of the EVs and the respective impact of these technology. Simulations will then be conducted to yield specific insights into the impact of V2G technology. Ultimately, the study aims to analyse strategies for sustainable grid management through ancillary service amidst the evolving landscape of transportation electrification.

articleTitle: Implementation of NMOS-based LDO Using Recycling Folded-Cascode in 16 nm FinFET
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a robust conventional NMOS-based Low Dropout Regulator (LDO) in 16nm FinFET. The LDO features a recycling folded-cascode as error amplifier with a supply voltage ranging from 1.028V to 1.32V and a programmable output voltage from 0.4V to 0.9V. The primary objective of this work is to achieve the optimal balance between various specifications including DC gain, Power Supply Rejection Ratio (PSRR), silicon area, and line/load regulation response. The robustness of the LDO design was thoroughly validated at the schematic level under 516 Process, Voltage, and Temperature (PVT) corners, as well as through Monte Carlo (MC) Simulations. The designed LDO, occupying an estimated area of 2696.8 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, demonstrates a mean DC gain of 74.87dB, PSRR at 10kHz of −76.28dB, and PSRR at 1MHz of −36.29db. Additionally, the LDO consistently maintains a phase margin exceeding 65°. The proposed LDO is compared with the current state of the art.

articleTitle: Specification of Complex Events and Their Integration in the IOPT-Tools Development Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: Controllers for discrete-event systems are typically designed using formalisms such as state diagrams and Petri nets. These formalisms rely heavily on the concept of events, which can represent anything from a simple change in signal value to more complex behavioral evolutions of signals. Modeling strategies including events allow model compactness and expressiveness. In this paper, a review on different types of input and output events associated with Boolean and multi-valued signals is presented. This paper presents their integration in the IOPT-Tools development environment, which uses a specific class of Petri nets for system’s modeling, the Input-Output Place-Transition nets (IOPT-nets). The IOPT-Tools development environment, accessible for free at http://gres.uninova.pt/IOPT-Tools/, offers a comprehensive environment enabling model creation and editing through the model editor, as well as testing and validation via tools such as the simulator and state space construction. Additionally, it supports the automatic execution code generation of these models (using C and VHDL) allowing the direct deployment on different types of platforms. The paper presents specific interfaces allowing the definition of complex events characteristics in the IOPT-Tools development environment and their usage in the context of discrete-event controllers development.

articleTitle: Development of a Power Electronics Interface between an Energy Storage System and the Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: Concerns related to reducing the environmental footprint triggered a great search for new sources, particularly renewable energy sources (RES). However, the high intermittency of the RES combined with the decentralized generation (DG) is causing a set of new challenges for power grids (PG). One possible solution to deal with this problem is the iteration of energy storage systems (ESS), namely battery energy storage systems (BESS), to store the excess energy during off peak hours, to be used during on peak hours. This paper proposes the power electronics converters to interface a BESS with the PG, based on a two-leg interleaved dc-dc bidirectional converter and a three-level dc-ac neutral point clamped inverter (NPC). Simulation results shows that with proposed topology it is possible to maintain a current with low ripple from the BESS side as well as with sinusoidal currents with very low total harmonic distortion (THD) from the PG side.

articleTitle: Implementation of an intelligent virtual assistant based on LLM models for irrigation optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: This paper explores the application of new AI capabilities and Large Languages Models (LLMs) in agriculture by developing an intelligent virtual assistant. The assistant aims to provide essential information on crops, vulnerabilities, and optimization strategies. The study focuses on implementing a robust pipeline architecture that trains LLMs for practical scenarios. This architecture ensures data and demonstrates substantial domain knowledge. Central to this approach is the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology, which organizes information into a streamlined format for efficient retrieval. Unlike fine-tuning methods, RAG separates base knowledge from the model, enabling a faster and more adapted pipeline. This proposal transforms retrieved information into an accessible format, facilitating rapid access to comprehensive agricultural expertise.

articleTitle: Horses Identification Through Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: In many horse-related events, such as competitions, auctions, international travel, or doping control, the need to determine the identity of all horses involved is a must to ensure transperecy or simple misidentification of the horses. To circumvent these problems, the possibility of creating a deep neural network to classify live footage of the horses seems promising, as it could potentially provide another layer of validation and be relatively hard to falsify compared to the methods currently used. This paper produced a dataset composed of 17 different horses and around 10500 images, and developed a network model, creating it based on the VGG-16 model, and gradually changing its complexity and adjusting its architecture in each iteration until reaching the final accuracy ranging from 97.15% to 99.89%.

articleTitle: Data Science for Geographic Information Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: The integration of data science into Geographic Information Systems (GIS) has facilitated the evolution of these tools into complete spatial analysis platforms. The adoption of machine learning and big data techniques has equipped these platforms with the capacity to handle larger amounts of increasingly complex data, transcending the limitations of more traditional approaches. This work traces the historical and technical evolution of data science and GIS as fields of study, highlighting the critical points of convergence between domains, and underlining the many sectors that rely on this integration. A GIS application is presented as a case study in the disaster management sector where we utilize aerial data from Tróia, Portugal, to emphasize the process of insight extraction from raw data. We conclude by outlining prospects for future research in integration of these fields in general, and the developed application in particular.

articleTitle: Adaptive Simulation of Separate Factors in the Alexandridis Wildfire Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: This paper provides a concise and comprehensive analysis of forest fire spread simulation. The Alexandridis model was implemented and enhanced utilizing stochastic methods in a Python environment. The impact of various factors influencing fire spread was individually studied. Results were empirically analyzed based on model-generated images, addressing the lack of real fire data. Multiple scenarios and parameter values were explored, highlighting the effectiveness of the developed method. In summary, this paper provides a concise and comprehensive analysis of forest fire spread simulation, demonstrating the efficacy of the Alexandridis model. Findings suggest the potential for developing a more effective model to combat forest fires and improve prediction and prevention methods.

articleTitle: Forest Height Estimation using Machine Learning Regressors with SAR Data
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: One of the most important forests’ characteristics is its height, which can give valuable knowledge for different purposes, such as its management, wildfire prevention, carbon stock estimation, or even helping in obtaining other indicators. Since forests are normally spread over extensive areas, it can be expensive and time-consuming to map all areas with precise measurements taken directly on the ground or airborne. A solution that has been studied over the last years is using satellite imagery to help map forests’ height. The purpose of this paper is to present how Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data, particularly from Sentinel-1, can improve the forest height estimation with Machine Learning (ML) regressors. First, an analysis of SAR’s Single Look Complex (SLC) data was performed to test how this data can provide similar results to Ground Range Detected (GRD) data. Then an analysis of how the results with GRD data can be improved with the use of Land Cover Land Use (LCLU) maps, specifically on the speckle filters usually applied. Finally, a combination of SLC and GRD data was tested, showing an improvement in the overall results of ML regressors, with a Stacking Regressor averaging a R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 70.39% and a relative RMSE of 21.44%. All the tests were performed on six regions of Portugal (and a few tests on ten more similar regions, from Spain and California), with data from six months in 2020.

articleTitle: Extending IOPT-Nets with High-Level Features: A Power Wheelchair Digital Twin Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: Petri nets are used across various domains for modeling systems with concurrent and asynchronous behavior. Its application extends to assessing the dependability and risk-related measures in these systems, improving their operational and safety requirements through analysis and re-design. In parallel, digital twins offer a promising approach to design, monitor, and control physical entities. Notably, non-autonomous Petri nets, such as Input-Output Place-Transition nets (IOPT-nets), prove suitable for modeling and deploying digital twins, relying on input and output signals to easily specify the interaction between the systems and the external world. This article proposes an extension of the IOPT-nets class to include additional high-level features to handle the implementation of digital twins in complex scenarios. The focus is on a case study involving the development of digital twins for power wheelchairs, which are systems that need to be safe and reliable to fulfill their purpose. Validation of these high-level features considers unfolding principles to ensure successful application within the IOPT-Tools framework.

articleTitle: AI generated route data pre - processing for faster decision making
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: The industry is constantly generating new data, allowing take advantage of their use to increase manufacturing efficiency through the reutilisation of operational times.One such possibility is to use Artificial Intelligence (AI). While AI is heralded as a solution for industry efficiency and accuracy quandaries through process automation, its implementation grapples with the issue of inaccurate production data used for training, giving an erroneous estimation.This article introduces a framework to facilitate the integration of AI tools within companies. The focus is on the accuracy of predicting normative times and selecting alternative routes when accuracy is low. This approach improves the price quotation prediction process, where using AI is practical due to time constraints. Making quick and accurate decisions is crucial for maintaining efficiency in production.To elucidate the functionality, the authors have performed a case study in production for the framework’s validation. The wood production sector was selected due to its lower operational complexity than machinery construction, resulting in time savings in the planning process.The study revealed that the prediction accuracy of AI was 70% on average for operations normative times. To improve this accuracy, the t-test method to classify operations was used. This approach eliminates operations with low AI prediction accuracy when making price quotations. Through the case study, AI module accuracy reached 80%, while the additional data collection volume decreased by one-third.

articleTitle: Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning System for Vehicular and Pedestrian Traffic Control with Visible Light Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering (YEF-ECE)
abstract: With the modernization of vehicles, new opportunities have emerged when it comes to automotive innovation. Due to the technological evolution of today’s new vehicles, it is possible for vehicles to be connected (CV) to each other, exchanging traffic and safety information.New communication technologies between vehicles and/or infrastructures can increase safety, and comfort while traveling. With a connected traffic environment, it is expected to obtain important information about the vehicular and pedestrian traffic flow in order to optimise it. Visible light communication (VLC) is then proposed as an integrated approach to optimize traffic flow at urban intersections.With this amount of information collected via VLC it is necessary to have a system that intelligently controls in real time all traffic and responds to all incoming vehicle’s manoeuvring requests. A two connected four-arm intersection scenario is considered. The simulation process involves using the SUMO urban mobility simulator. A multi agent reinforcement learning system, with a Deep Q-Learning algorithm is used to control both intersections, optimising traffic flows and minimise congestion during peak hours. A comparative analysis of the simulation results highlights the benefits of the proposed approach in terms of throughput, reducing delays and minimising vehicle stops, revealing improved patterns for optimising signals and trajectories.
